subject: Assigning the value of numericInput depending on a radioButton or selectList choice

messages.author: d49d81f49c53329e
messages.subject: Assigning the value of numericInput depending on a radioButton or selectList choice
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to put together a system where, upon the choice of an item from a selectList or radioButton, the values of some numericInput are altered, hence causing everything depending on that to be re-executed.

I thought the right way to do this would be to use the conditionalPanel in this way:

selectInput(inputId='Physiology', label='Choose a species/physiology', choices=c('Rat','Mouse'), multiple=F, selected='Rat'),
    shiny::conditionalPanel(
      condition="input.Physiology == 'Rat'", 
      numericInput("GI_length", "GI_length (m):", .1, step=.1),
      numericInput("GI_radius", "GI_radius (m):", .0018, step=.0001),
      numericInput("GI_TrTime", "GI_TrTime (mins):", 5)
    ),
    shiny::conditionalPanel(
      condition="input.Physiology == 'Mouse'", 
      numericInput("GI_length", "GI_length (m):", .04, step=.01),
      numericInput("GI_radius", "GI_radius (m):", .0006, step=.0001),
      numericInput("GI_TrTime", "GI_TrTime (mins):", 15)
    ),

However, although this gives me the kind of interface I am looking for, it doesn't work since the reactivity is attached only to the first instance of the different numericInput with the same inputId. The model re-evaluates correctly when the 'rat' option is selected, in the specific case, and I modify any of the three numericInput. However, if I select 'Mouse', and change the values in that panel, nothing happens.

Any suggestions on how to get out of this impasse? Is there a way to 'write' values to a numericInput in a reactive way, depending from the choice of a selectList? So that I can export them out of the conditionalPanel, and avoid having more than one with the same inputID?

Thanks for any feedback,

Luca

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Assigning the value of numericInput depending on a radioButton or selectList choice
parts:
The issue is that conditionalPanels are merely hidden when the condition is false. So both the Rat and Mouse conditionalPanel are always on the web page - it's just that one of them is visible.

If you're using Chrome, you can inspect the structure of the web page by right-clicking on the element and selecting "Inspect Element". I've attached an image of what it looks like when inspecting your page. As you can see, both Mouse and Rat are there.

To work around it, you can use dynamic UI. For an example, see:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/dynamic_ui/
Source code at:
  https://gist.github.com/4211337

And the tutorial page at:
  http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#dynamic-ui

-Winston
